claims.text: Optimized cold-spray deposition of CoCrFeNiMo HEA powder onto damaged stainless steel will produce a dense coating.
The cold-sprayed coating will have an ultrafine-grained microstructure.
The intervention will significantly improve surface hardness relative to fusion-welded repairs and untreated stainless steel.
The intervention will significantly improve wear resistance relative to fusion-welded repairs and untreated stainless steel.
The intervention will significantly improve corrosion resistance in aggressive environments relative to fusion-welded repairs and untreated stainless steel.
Cold-spray repair will eliminate hot cracking relative to traditional fusion-welding repair.
The target damaged stainless-steel components possess microstructural defects that predispose them to hot cracking during traditional repair.
Pre-cleaning and light roughening of the stainless-steel substrate will support successful cold-spray deposition.
Tuning particle velocity and standoff distance can ensure uniform bonding, including on complex geometries.
No post-deposition heat treatment is required.
The coating forms a metallurgical bond with the substrate through severe plastic deformation during high-velocity particle impact.
High-velocity particle impact causes adiabatic shear.
Impact-induced deformation and adiabatic shear refine the coating grain structure.
Cold spraying produces bonding without entering the melting regime.
Avoiding melting prevents the thermal stresses that lead to hot cracking.
The impact-induced coating structure concurrently enhances wear and corrosion resistance.
Cold-spray repair is expected to be effective on flat or moderately curved surfaces, while extremely complex geometries may require further parameter refinement.
A less than 20% increase in surface hardness and durability metrics relative to both controls is specified as a falsifying result.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says cold spraying will eliminate hot cracking, whereas the predicted outcome only claims a markedly reduced incidence of hot cracking.
